title: Directions EMEA 2026 Reflections
summary: Reflections on organizing Directions EMEA 2026, covering session selection from 800+ submissions, conference logistics, and the Developer Zone roundtables. The post shares insights on AI in development, open-source adoption, DevOps trends, and the growing Business Central community.
key_points: Session selection from 800+ submissions balanced audiences, speakers and diversity; the average session score rose to 4.51 from 4.49 the year before
AI agents are already giving partners efficiency and quality gains, but developers stay responsible for AI-written AL and need ways to verify it
AL-Go for GitHub is gaining popularity as a partner DevOps choice, and Microsoft is committed to supporting it
Microsoft has open-sourced the Base Application, System Application and localizations but not the platform; open-source projects need maintenance, support and sponsorship
A roundtable concluded that the most valuable future Business Central professional may be a solution architect with development skills and deep business process knowledge

quotes.text: you're responsible for what you ship, so you need a way to verify AI's work. Without that, you're running blindfolded through a minefield.
quotes.why_it_matters: Highlights the critical requirement for validation and ownership when using AI to generate AL code, addressing a key concern in modern development practices

quotes.text: AI agents are here. Partners who know how to use them are already seeing gains in efficiency, performance, and quality.
quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes that AI agents are now a practical tool in production use among Business Central partners with measurable business benefits
